# Interpretation v2 — issue #952: token-position-resolved on/off-policy characterization of the context→answer activation map + divergence-conditioned evaluation

Revision of `epm:interpretation v1` addressing the full union of both round-1 critiques (leg-1 control accuracy, H1 layer scoping, bank cap-length prevalence, H3 scope + instrument caveats, spans-verification surface, per-hypothesis confidence split, surprisal phrasing, H2 cell scoping, t128 style read, full-set transfer floor, #823 quantitative anchor, hero2/hero3 label regeneration). Body promotion still deferred (no set-body / set-title / set-clean-result this pass).

**Headline:** the off-policy (external-answer) predictability penalty in the frozen ridge context→answer-activation map is **position-uniform, not opening-concentrated, at the validation-selected read-out layer ℓ\*=20** (H1 falsified with an affirmative equivalence read, scoped to that layer; 40/42 position slots independently select L20 in the layer-sensitivity diagnostic); for **plain external answers the penalty closes entirely at the registered decision cell (L20, 16-token prefix)** — it does NOT replicate at the non-registered L17 (+0.0136, CI spans 0), so the closure is a registered-cell finding, not a layer-general one — and it reverses for the distinct-style arm (the style penalty persists through 128 absorbed tokens); and on the **surviving identity/style divergence bank** (2 of 4 planned categories; judge calibration inverted and the adjusted pair keep-margin was effectively vacuous — instrument caveats that attach to every H3 statement below) **no divergence-specific external failure was detected at the registered 0.05 margin**, an informative non-detection in the reachability sense (conditional ceiling 0.887 far exceeds the null band's 97.5% bound +0.028). Net read: prediction from context is content/prefix-indexed at the read-out layer, sharpening the parent line quantitatively — [#823](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/823) measured plain-style external answers retaining 91–98% of own-answer refit R² at the answer-mean level (97.6% evil / 91.4% sycophancy / 94.4% hallucination; mismatched ≈ 0); this run resolves the residual own-advantage as small (~0.02 pooled R²), flat across answer positions at ℓ\*=20, and absorbed by a 16-token prefix for plain answers — with one new wrinkle, a persistent style penalty that prefix absorption does not close.

Codex is right; the exemption sentence is both an unlicensed exemption FORM and factually over-broad, so the promotion record cannot carry it.

Exemptions, stated in the interpretation prose or alt text: the result's primary figure ALREADY is the per-unit view (a raw scatter needs no second scatter); N is so small the figure already shows every point; or the aggregate has no meaningful per-unit decomposition (a single scalar)." That is a closed 3-item list. Result 4's line — "Per-unit exemption: these cells aggregate the same per-context arrays underlying the prefix-closure ECDF above — this read's per-unit surface; another panel would replot them." — invokes a FOURTH form (coverage by a per-unit figure living in a DIFFERENT `### <result>`), which the #480 cross-H4-pointer precedent and the #923 r2 reconcile both adjudicated as not the carve-out. ## Honest narrative

1. **The equivalence finding is layer-general across the captured band; its "at the selected read-out layer" qualifier was wrong.** Position-uniformity of the own-answer advantage replicates at every layer read (14/20/23/26). The correct scoping is BAND-scoped, not universal: early layers {2, 6, 10} were excluded at the predictability noise floor (≤ 0.057) and L27 was never captured — this is same-run captured-band support, not three independent replications. Headline retitle: "position-uniform across the captured read-out layer band."
2. **The closure finding is layer-fragile and becomes a mid-band phenomenon.** Under the registered absolute criterion: affirmatively absent at L14, replicating at L20 (parent) and L23, indeterminate at L26, non-replicating at L17 (parent). The fraction-of-own-gap read (plan guidance) sharpens rather than rescues this: 16 absorbed tokens close 75–108% of the layer's own 0-prefix gap at layers 17–23 but only 15–18% at the band edges 14 and 26.
3. **Scale-vs-locality, weighed per guidance.** At L14 the ±0.03/0.02 margins are ≈ 38% of the layer's 0.079 predictability (vs 28% at L20), and the L14 0-prefix gap (0.0128) is itself BELOW the 0.02 closure margin — the `replicates` conjunct was unreachable there by construction, so the affirmative status alone cannot carry a locality claim. The fraction read is the right conditioning, and it AGREES: 15% closure at L14 is genuine non-closure, not a margin artifact. (L17's carried "non-replication" is the one read the fraction view reinterprets: 78% of its own gap closes; its absolute failure is largely scale-driven, since even complete closure of a 0.0174 gap could not reach 0.02.) L23 is the matched-scale discriminator (predictability 0.090, ~15% below L20; 0-prefix gap 0.027 ≥ L20's 0.023) and it REPLICATES — so the closure mechanism is not an L20-selection artifact. L26 is the scale-matched edge case (gap 0.028) where closure is small (18%) but the read is indeterminate, not affirmative.
4. **What this does to the parent story:** the small own-answer advantage is a band-wide, position-uniform property; the prefix-absorption closure of the plain-external part of that advantage is concentrated in the mid band (17–23), fading toward both captured edges — with the edge reads split between one affirmative absence (L14, low-scale) and one indeterminate (L26). A purely local-readout account of the closure is rejected (it replicates at a second, matched-scale layer); a fully layer-general account is also rejected (affirmative absence at L14). The style-gap non-closure and the divergence-bank null are layer-stable.
5. **Alternatives considered:** (a) new-code artifact — excluded by the suffixed-L20 calibration gate (exact reproduction of known answers through the new path); (b) λ mis-tuning at added layers — excluded by per-layer re-selection under the parent's registered rule; (c) selection-on-max — no cross-layer max anywhere, fixed pre-registered layer set; (d) multiple comparisons — Holm across the three added layers per family, raw + adjusted reported; the L23 closure verdict is not correction-sensitive; (e) scale confound — addressed via the fraction-of-own-gap companion above.

1. **The equivalence finding is layer-general across the captured band; its "at the selected read-out layer" qualifier was wrong — but only the position-UNIFORMITY is layer-general, not the SIZE.** Position-uniformity of the own-answer advantage replicates at every layer read (14/20/23/26); the advantage's magnitude is layer-dependent, ~0.01–0.03 R² growing with depth (≈0.02–0.03 at the selected layer 20; the L14 gaps are 0.0102/0.0163 first/last-16 and 0.0128 at 0-prefix). The correct scoping is BAND-scoped, not universal: early layers {2, 6, 10} were excluded at the predictability noise floor (≤ 0.057) and L27 was never captured — this is same-run captured-band support, not three independent replications. Headline retitle: "position-uniform across the captured read-out layer band."
2. **The closure finding is layer-fragile and concentrates in the mid band.** Under the registered absolute criterion: affirmatively absent at L14, replicating at L20 (parent) and L23, indeterminate at L26, non-replicating at L17 (parent). The fraction-of-own-gap read (plan guidance) sharpens this: 16 absorbed tokens close 75–108% of the layer's own 0-prefix gap at layers 17–23; at the edges the point estimates are 15% (L14, affirmatively below the absolute margin) and 18% (L26, indeterminate — never pool the two: one is an affirmative absence, the other unresolved).
3. **Scale-vs-locality, weighed per guidance.** At L14 the ±0.03/0.02 margins are ≈ 38% of the layer's 0.079 predictability (vs 28% at L20), and the L14 0-prefix gap (0.0128) is itself BELOW the 0.02 closure margin — the `replicates` conjunct was unreachable there by construction, so the affirmative status alone cannot carry a locality claim. The fraction read stays descriptive on this point: the closure point estimate is small (≈15% of a gap that is itself only 0.013), but the ΔG CI upper (+0.0162) exceeds the whole t0 gap (0.0128), so full fractional closure is compatible with the data — the absolute-margin non-replication at L14 is scale-conditioned, not an affirmed locality boundary. (L17's carried "non-replication" is the read the fraction view most clearly reinterprets: 78% of its own gap closes; its absolute failure is largely scale-driven, since even complete closure of a 0.0174 gap could not reach 0.02.) L23 is the matched-scale discriminator (predictability 0.090, ~15% below L20; 0-prefix gap 0.027 ≥ L20's 0.023) and it REPLICATES — so the closure mechanism is not an L20-selection artifact. L26 is the scale-matched edge case (gap 0.028) where the closure point estimate is small (18%) but the read is indeterminate, not affirmative.
4. **What this does to the parent story:** the small own-answer advantage is a band-wide, position-uniform property whose size grows with depth; the prefix-absorption closure of the plain-external part of that advantage concentrates in the mid band (17–23), with the edge reads split — affirmatively absent at L14 (low-scale), unresolved at L26. A purely local-readout account of the closure is rejected (it replicates at a second, matched-scale layer); a fully layer-general account is also rejected (affirmative absence at L14). The style-gap closure point estimates are negative at every layer (affirmed at L14 and the parent's L17; zero-spanning elsewhere), and the L14 position read independently shows the style gap widening along the answer (contrast −0.0164, raw p 0.0004); the divergence-bank null is layer-stable.
5. **Alternatives considered:** (a) new-code artifact — excluded by the suffixed-L20 calibration gate (exact reproduction of known answers through the new path); (b) λ mis-tuning at added layers — excluded by per-layer re-selection under the parent's registered rule; (c) selection-on-max — no cross-layer max anywhere, fixed pre-registered layer set; (d) multiple comparisons — Holm across the three added layers per family, raw + adjusted reported; the L23 closure verdict is not correction-sensitive; (e) scale confound — addressed via the fraction-of-own-gap companion above, which cuts BOTH ways: it reinterprets L17's absolute failure and it keeps the L14 fractional read point-estimate-only.
